RE: Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-C3B5D8F398-85355
Member: Sawyer Delgado
Requested Service: CPT 63030 — lumbar laminotomy/hemilaminectomy with decompression of nerve root(s)
Date of Denial Notice: 2026-08-13
Treating Surgeon: Lindqvist, MD, Orthopedic Surgery

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am writing to formally appeal the denial of prior authorization for CPT 63030, as set forth in the notice referenced above. This appeal is submitted within the 180-day window stated in the notice (deadline 2027-02-09).

**Stated reason for denial**

The notice states: "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure." I ask the reviewer to reconsider this determination in light of the complete clinical record, summarized below, which was not fully reflected in the initial review.

**Governing policy**

Based on my own research, Anthem/Empire administers prior authorization for spine surgery, including CPT 63030, under Carelon Medical Benefits Management's "Clinical Appropriateness Guidelines — Musculoskeletal Appropriate Use Criteria: Spine Surgery." The version of that guideline in effect on the date of this denial identifies itself, in the document I retrieved directly, as follows: "Status: Revised Effective Date: 11/15/2025 Doc ID: MSK03-1125.1 Last Review Date: 01/30/2025." That document's table of contents lists a dedicated section titled "Lumbar Discectomy, Foraminotomy, and Laminotomy" beginning at page 27, with subsections "Description and Scope," "Clinical Indications," "Exclusions," "References," and "Codes."

The "Description and Scope" portion of that section, as I retrieved it, states: "This guideline addresses lumbar discectomy, foraminotomy, and laminotomy when performed as elective, non-emergent procedures and not as part of the care of an acute or traumatic event," and "Lumbar discectomy involves removal of the disc, in whole or part. Foraminotomy and laminotomy involve removal of a portion of the lamina (bony arch) on the dorsal surface of a vertebra."

I was not able to retrieve the complete, current "Clinical Indications" bullet list for this section directly from the live document (it is a long, multi-condition PDF). I therefore do not put the detailed indications criteria below in quotation marks, and I am not attributing quoted language to the plan for that list. What I can state is that a predecessor version of this same Carelon guideline (effective 2024-10-20 to 2025-11-14) — which Carelon's own published update summary indicates was revised for later dates only to change narrative text tied to CPT codes 22632 and 22634 (unrelated fusion codes), not to the discectomy/foraminotomy/laminotomy indications — described medically necessary indications for this procedure in terms of radicular pain or nerve findings correlating to imaging, together with either an urgent neurologic presentation or a documented trial of conservative treatment. I ask that the reviewer confirm, and apply, whatever the exact current wording of that "Clinical Indications" subsection is when re-evaluating this claim, and that the reviewer provide me a copy of the specific criteria applied to this member's request, as is my right.

Separately, in the current document, I directly retrieved the following general provision applicable across the spine-surgery guideline: "The requirement for a period of conservative management as a prerequisite to a surgical procedure is waived when there is evidence of progressive nerve or spinal cord compression resulting in a significant neurologic deficit, or when cauda equina syndrome or conus medullaris syndrome is present." I raise this because, even independent of any conservative-care analysis, this member's presentation includes a documented neurologic deficit at the imaged level.

**How the clinical record addresses the stated denial reason**

1. **Imaging directly demonstrates the pathology at issue.** MRI of the lumbar spine dated 2026-06-30 shows an L4-L5 disc extrusion with severe right lateral recess stenosis and compression of the traversing L5 nerve root. This is a structural, radiographically severe finding — not an equivocal or incidental one — and it corresponds anatomically to the member's clinical presentation described below. The stated denial reason, that "the imaging findings submitted do not support medical necessity," does not address why a severe, nerve-root-compressing disc extrusion at the symptomatic level would be insufficient, and I ask that the reviewer identify specifically what additional imaging finding is believed to be missing.

2. **The imaging correlates with the clinical and examination findings.** The record documents radicular pain radiating into the right calf, a distribution consistent with the L5 nerve root shown to be compressed on MRI; positive provocative testing on the affected side; and a neurologic deficit corresponding to the imaged level. This is the kind of imaging-to-clinical correlation that spine-surgery necessity review is intended to confirm, and it is present here.

3. **Conservative treatment was tried, was adequate in duration, and failed.** The member completed 24 supervised physical therapy visits over 10 weeks (2026-04-10 to 2026-06-19), including core stabilization and lumbar flexibility work, as documented in the physical therapy discharge note. The member also completed 4 months of NSAID therapy with inadequate relief, and received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-04-14 that produced only 3 weeks of partial relief. Symptoms have now been progressive for 9 months and unrelieved by rest. Whatever specific duration of "conservative management" the current Clinical Indications subsection requires, this course of physical therapy, medication, and injection substantially exceeds any minimal duration referenced in the predecessor version of this guideline, and it has failed to resolve the member's symptoms.

4. **Functional impact is significant.** The member cannot stand for more than 10 minutes without symptom exacerbation and continues to have radicular pain into the right calf despite the treatment above. This is the kind of "significant functional impairment" that the guideline's indications for surgery are directed at.

5. **No disqualifying factors are present.** The record reflects no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and non-smoker status — none of which raises a surgical contraindication or fits within any exclusion criterion of the "Exclusions" subsection referenced in the Carelon Spine Surgery guideline (I have not been able to retrieve the specific text of that subsection and am not quoting it; I note only that nothing in this record suggests these exclusions apply).

**Requested action**

I ask that Anthem/Empire:

1. Overturn the denial and authorize CPT 63030 as requested by Dr. Lindqvist;
2. If the denial is not fully overturned on this written appeal, provide the complete, current text of the "Clinical Indications" subsection of the "Lumbar Discectomy, Foraminotomy, and Laminotomy" section of the Carelon Spine Surgery guideline (Doc ID MSK03-1125.1) that was actually applied to this determination, so that the specific criterion said not to be met can be addressed directly;
3. Offer a peer-to-peer conversation between the plan's medical reviewer and Dr. Lindqvist before any further determination; and
4. Treat this appeal as urgent/expedited given the member's ongoing radicular pain, functional limitation, and neurologic findings.

Enclosed with this appeal are copies of: the MRI report dated 2026-06-30; the physical therapy discharge note (24 visits, 2026-04-10 to 2026-06-19); records of NSAID therapy and the corticosteroid injection dated 2026-04-14; and the surgeon's office notes documenting examination findings and neurologic deficit.

If this internal appeal is not resolved in the member's favor, I understand I retain the right to pursue an independent external appeal through New York State (NY Department of Financial Services), and I reserve that right.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address above, or to [preferred phone/email — not contained in the records provided].

Sincerely,

Sawyer Delgado
